name: Thai citizenship by naturalisation (Nationality Act B.E. 2508)

requirement_groups.name: General track, 5 years' permanent residence, points test

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding permanent residence status for at least 5 consecutive years, per Section 10 of the Nationality Act B.E. 2508.
requirements.fix_path: Continue holding permanent residence for the required 5-year period (see th_permanent_residence).

requirements.blocker_text: Requires scoring at least 50 of 100 points on the citizenship points test (applicable to marriage-based and PR-based applicants; a separate, different process applies to women applying via a Thai husband), covering qualifications (up to 25 points) plus other assessed categories including conversational Thai proficiency, good conduct, and having a regular occupation with a valid work permit.
requirements.fix_path: Build toward the 50-point threshold across the qualifications, language, conduct, and occupation categories.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicants are typically expected to speak and understand conversational Thai and may be asked to sing the Thai National Anthem and the Royal Anthem during the citizenship interview, alongside a clean criminal record requirement.
requirements.fix_path: Prepare to demonstrate conversational Thai and knowledge of the National and Royal Anthems at interview.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' continuous permanent residence status
Points-test documentation covering qualifications, occupation, and conduct
Valid work permit and regular-occupation proof

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: final approval requires Royal assent under the Nationality Act, a genuine additional procedural stage beyond ministry-level processing

sources.title: LegalClarity -- Thailand Permanent Residence: Requirements and Process, citing Section 10 of the Nationality Act B.E. 2508 for the 5-year PR-to-naturalisation requirement and describing the National/Royal Anthem interview component

HONEST SOURCING GAP: no direct fetch of a Ministry of Interior or Royal Thai Government Gazette page was achieved for the Nationality Act's primary statutory text or the points-test's official criteria document in this research pass -- both sources are specialist tier-3 guides, though the points-test source specifically reproduces what it presents as the official Thai-language scoring rubric verbatim, giving somewhat higher confidence than a typical secondary summary. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the points-test mechanism (50-of-100 threshold, covering qualifications, language, conduct, and occupation) applies specifically to PR-based and marriage-based (via a Thai wife) applicants -- a woman applying for citizenship via a Thai husband follows a different, separately-documented process not modeled in this route given research-depth limits in this pass, flagged as a candidate for future expansion. The requirement to sing the Thai National Anthem and Royal Anthem during the citizenship interview is a genuinely distinctive cultural-integration test not seen in comparable form elsewhere in this dataset -- closer in spirit to Denmark's mandatory Grundlovsceremoni handshake than to a written civics exam, though assessed conversationally rather than via a formal certified test. Final naturalisation approval requires Royal assent, a genuine additional procedural layer beyond ministry-level decision-making -- structurally comparable to Denmark's Act-of-Parliament citizenship mechanism documented elsewhere in this dataset, in that neither country treats naturalisation as a purely administrative act, though Thailand's mechanism runs through the monarchy rather than the legislature specifically. dual_citizenship_allowed is modeled true based on general knowledge that Thailand does not require renunciation of prior nationality for naturalised citizens in most cases, but this was not independently verified against a primary source in this specific research pass and should be treated as the best available answer rather than a fully confirmed fact.
